lines.text: A train now runs under the sea, from Europe to Asia.
Istanbul sits on two continents, split by the Bosphorus.
So how do you get a railway under the sea?
The deepest point sits near sixty meters down.
They only sank a section when the current ran under three knots.
First, they cast eleven sections. Each one is longer than a football pitch.
Then each section was towed to the strait.
Crews dredged a trench about fourteen meters down.
Then it was lowered, slowly, as its tanks took in water.
Machines levelled gravel, and grout filled the gaps.
Rubber gaskets seal each joint, and the water is pumped out.
At each shore, the tube links to bored tunnels in the hills.
Joined end to end, the tube is one thousand, three hundred eighty seven meters.
Europe to Asia, built one piece at a time.
